company.name: Coalesce.io
company.industry: Data transformation SaaS for the Snowflake ecosystem
company.icp_fit: A — primary ICP (130 emp, cloud-native, sensitive customer data, no named security owner)

routing_rationale: Builder-CTO archetype, technical co-founder. The four picks at Coalesce split: Satish (architecture / build-vs-buy), Mike McCune VP Eng (capacity-gap / sprint tax), Justin Stanford Director Infra (drift), Cyrille David Head of Eng (CI-runtime collapse). Satish gets the build-vs-buy framing because that is the canonical builder-CTO conversation.

research_summary.trigger_event: Coalesce's enterprise customer mix in the Snowflake ecosystem skews toward financial services and healthcare; SOC 2 evidence + access lineage on a continuous cadence is the recurring procurement ask at this stage
research_summary.what_we_know: Co-founded Coalesce with Armon Petrossian. Series B closed 2024. Coalesce is the GUI-driven dbt-alternative for Snowflake. No security-titled person in the source contact set — security ownership likely sits across the founding team and infra leadership, common at this stage.

draft.body:
No security-titled owner in the public footprint reads less as gap and more as deliberate at 130 people — until enterprise prospects in financial services and healthcare ask for SOC 2 evidence and access-lineage on a cadence the founding team can't manufacture without standing up a function. The build-vs-buy at this stage isn't whether to hire a CISO; it's whether the continuous evidence can be a property of how the platform runs.

Transilience does that part — declared baseline, continuous drift detection, prioritized findings, remediation with humans in the loop — so the team you do have spends its time on judgment, not screenshots.

Worth fifteen minutes if the framing maps?
draft.voice_register_used: dry-precise (with mild diagnostic-pattern in the opener)
draft.architecture: signal-to-question, with the signal being the absence of a named security owner and the question being the build-vs-buy reframe

witness.what_works: Opener reframes the absence as deliberate before naming the cost — gives the reader credit before naming the wound. Build-vs-buy framing is the canonical builder-CTO move from craft/personas/cto.md and lands without product positioning. The product sentence is one sentence, names the loop concretely (Declare/Detect/Decide/Deliver paraphrased without brand-jargon), and earns its place by following the build-vs-buy reframe. CTA is short and not begging.
witness.what_fails: The opener is opinionated — 'reads less as gap and more as deliberate' is a judgment that could feel presumptuous to a co-founder whose security strategy I have not fully read. Mitigation: the sentence completes by naming the trigger ('until enterprise prospects ask...'), which converts the opener from judgment to observation. Watch reply tone for whether this lands or grates.
